article: Salesforce Chatter投稿の整理方法とストレージの注意点
scope: Compared the full Japanese article and all twelve translations, including storage claims, SOQL, object scope, permissions, reversibility, file-share effects, instructions, metadata, and official references.
findings: Removed the duplicate future date and retained 2022-09-19 as publication date; set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Corrected the premise: Chatter posts, comments, and tracked changes do not count toward data storage; files are counted separately as file storage.
Removed unfiltered DML deleting every FeedItem, FeedAttachment, and ContentDocument, as well as the org-wide Recycle Bin purge.
Replaced destructive code with a read-only ContentPost FeedItem query and a backup, sandbox, review, approval, and selected-ID Data Loader workflow aligned with Salesforce Help.
Warned that FeedItem deletion may be hard delete and explained that removing a Chatter attachment from a post does not guarantee the underlying file is purged from all locations.
Added Salesforce official references on storage categories and safe bulk cleanup.

post/Salesforceチャッター全消しコマンド/index.en.md.source: post/Salesforceチャッター全消しコマンド/index.md
post/Salesforceチャッター全消しコマンド/index.en.md.summary: Compared the complete Japanese article and twelve translations with Salesforce documentation; corrected the storage premise, removed unfiltered destructive Apex, and replaced it with a read-only review query and an approved, scoped Data Loader workflow.

meaning.note: Verified that Chatter posts/comments/tracked changes do not count toward data storage while files count toward file storage; clarified that deleting all posts does not resolve data-storage pressure.

terminology.note: Checked Chatter FeedItem, ContentPost, attachments, Data Loader, Workbench, Recycle Bin, data versus file storage, Storage Usage, and deletion permissions across all locales.

mathematics.note: This Salesforce operations guide contains no mathematical formulas or calculations.

code.note: Replaced unfiltered DML and recycle-bin purge commands with a read-only FeedItem query filtered to Type=ContentPost; documented export, review, backup, sandbox test, approval, and scoped Data Loader deletion.

links.note: Checked Salesforce Help and Developer references on Chatter storage, data/file storage usage, bulk deletion of attachment posts, FeedItem deletion, and file behavior in Chatter feeds.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The export/delete workflow was not run in a Salesforce org; permissions, org configuration, and data-specific retention requirements must be confirmed by the organization.
Deleting a FeedItem can be irreversible; whether a file remains at its original location or other shares depends on its state.
